edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. At Closing, the Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 (the “Base Purchase Price”), subject to adjustment as set forth herein, by wire transfer of immediately available funds. The amount payable at Closing shall be increased by the amount of Company cash and cash equivalents as of the Closing and decreased by Company indebtedness as of the Closing and by the amount, if any, by which Closing Net Working Capital is below the agreed target Net Working Capital (and increased by the amount, if any, by which Closing Net Working Capital exceeds that target), in each case determined in accordance with accounting principles and procedures to be agreed by the parties and consistently applied. The parties shall agree on the target Net Working Capital, the definition of indebtedness, and a post-Closing statement and review process in the definitive agreement. At Closing, the Buyer shall deposit 5% of the Base Purchase Price into escrow with an agreed escrow agent to secure the Seller’s indemnification obligations, with any undisputed balance released to the Seller 12 months after Closing. No amount shall be withheld or set off except as expressly provided in the definitive agreement.
edits.name: Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 2. Closing; Due Diligence. Closing shall occur within 30 days after execution of the definitive agreement, subject to satisfaction or waiver of the closing conditions. The Buyer shall have 30 days after execution of the definitive agreement to complete its due diligence. The Buyer’s obligation to proceed is conditioned on its satisfactory completion of due diligence, with the Buyer acting reasonably and in good faith and delivering written notice of any election not to proceed before the end of that period; if it does not timely deliver such notice, this condition shall be deemed satisfied. The definitive agreement shall include customary cooperation and access provisions, subject to applicable law, privilege, confidentiality, and reasonable operational safeguards.
edits.name: Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 3. Seller Representations. In the definitive agreement, the Seller shall make customary representations, subject to negotiated disclosure schedules and appropriate materiality and knowledge qualifiers, including as to: (a) organization, good standing, authority, and enforceability; (b) capitalization and ownership of the Shares; (c) the accuracy of the financial statements provided to the Buyer in all material respects; (d) absence of undisclosed liabilities, subject to customary exceptions; (e) compliance with applicable law; (f) material contracts; (g) litigation; (h) taxes; (i) employees and employee benefit matters; and (j) good title to the Shares, free and clear of liens created by the Seller. The definitive agreement shall also include customary representations concerning brokers and other matters agreed by the parties.
edits.name: Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement and all nonpublic information exchanged in connection with the transaction are confidential, subject to customary exceptions for disclosures to representatives, as required by law, and with the other party’s prior written consent.
edits.name: Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 5. Covenants. The definitive agreement shall include customary pre-Closing covenants, including operation of the Company in the ordinary course, reasonable access and information-sharing, notice of specified developments, and cooperation in obtaining required consents, in each case subject to agreed exceptions, applicable law, and the Buyer’s reasonable consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed. The Seller shall not be required to make any payment or assume any obligation to obtain a consent.
edits.name: Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 6. Closing Conditions. The Buyer’s obligation to close shall be conditioned on (a) the accuracy of the Seller’s representations and warranties at signing and Closing, subject to customary materiality qualifiers and an agreed materiality standard, (b) the Seller’s performance in all material respects of its covenants, (c) no injunction prohibiting the transaction, (d) receipt of agreed governmental approvals, and (e) delivery of customary closing documents. The Seller’s obligation to close shall be conditioned on the Buyer’s representations being accurate in all material respects, the Buyer’s performance in all material respects of its covenants, no injunction prohibiting the transaction, and the Buyer’s delivery of the closing consideration and customary closing documents. Conditions shall be subject to customary waiver provisions.
edits.name: Aldous Finch LLP

edits.text: 7. Indemnification. The definitive agreement shall provide for customary indemnification for breaches of representations, warranties, and covenants, subject to an exclusive-recourse framework and negotiated procedures. General representations shall survive for 12 months after Closing; fundamental representations concerning authority, capitalization, and title to the Shares shall survive for the applicable statute of limitations. Claims for general representation breaches shall be subject to a deductible basket equal to 1% of the Base Purchase Price and an aggregate cap equal to 10% of the Base Purchase Price; claims for fundamental representation breaches shall be subject to an aggregate cap equal to the Base Purchase Price. These limitations shall not apply to fraud. Recovery for general representation claims shall be made from the escrow to the extent available, and the definitive agreement shall include customary notice, mitigation, and no-double-recovery provisions. The parties shall negotiate any additional specific indemnities, if warranted by diligence.
edits.name: Aldous Finch LLP

receiver.requested_changes: Please revise the draft to reflect a $40,000,000 Base Purchase Price, subject to a clearly defined cash/debt/net-working-capital adjustment, with the target and accounting rules agreed before signing and a balanced post-closing preparation, review, and dispute-resolution process. The Buyer’s diligence condition should remain available through the diligence period without being deemed satisfied by failure to give notice; any notice should be effective if delivered before expiry, and the Buyer’s election should not be constrained by a reasonableness standard. Please add customary, robust access and cooperation obligations. Expand the Seller’s representations to cover, among other matters, authority, capitalization, financial statements, liabilities, compliance, contracts, litigation, taxes, employees and benefits, brokers, and title, with tailored rather than blanket materiality and knowledge qualifiers and appropriate disclosure schedules. For indemnification, propose a 10% escrow held for at least 18 months, a tipping basket (not a deductible), and a general cap no lower than the escrow amount; fundamental and specified indemnity claims should have appropriately longer survival and separate caps. Preserve direct recovery for claims not satisfied from escrow, and include customary claims procedures and fraud carve-outs. Please also identify any diligence-related specific indemnities the Seller is prepared to discuss.
